plans.note: Cap in 21.1 is mutual at greater of 12-month Fees or USD 1,000,000; check adequacy versus contract value (note the USD 2M/yr commitment in 2.1) and confirm Excluded Claims in 21.3 cover confidentiality, data/security, indemnities, gross negligence/wilful misconduct, IP and payment obligations. 21.2 already treats data restoration and incident response as direct damages.

No indemnification section appears in the outline, yet 9.3 references 'the remedies required by Section 20.5' and 21.3 and 30.5 assume indemnification obligations and indemnified parties. Flag the missing Vendor IP/misconduct indemnity and the broken cross-reference; anchor near sec-9.3 / sec-21.3.

Second 12.4 imposes a 24-month, all-territory non-compete on Customer — strike outright as contrary to playbook. It also conflicts with 12.3, which disclaims any exclusivity or non-compete commitment; cite that inconsistency.

12.3 preserves our freedom to source elsewhere (favourable, keep). Practical exclusivity pressure arises from 7.2 (match-or-disclose before engaging another provider) and the take-or-pay minimum in 2.1; address both.

First 7.2 is a reverse MFN requiring us to disclose and match third-party offers to Vendor — wrong direction, delete. Note 12.3 expressly denies any most-favoured-customer commitment, supporting removal.

First 12.4 bars soliciting, hiring or employing any Vendor employee for 24 months with no general-advertising carve-out and regardless of how they apply — narrow to 12 months, direct solicitation only, with a general-advertisement/unsolicited-applicant carve-out; reconcile with 12.3.

Section 9 contains only for-cause, insolvency and security/SLA termination (note there is no 9.4 in the outline); no Customer termination-for-convenience right. Add convenience termination on notice at sec-9 level, and reconcile with 2.1's 'without reduction or termination rights'.

8.2 (30-day non-renewal notice plus 60-day reminder with deadline extension) and 8.3 (uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3%, 90 days' notice) are largely playbook-compliant; verify only Customer-side notice burden and prepaid-period protection.

28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction — outside the accepted list and directly contradicts 28.2's exclusive New York County venue. Replace 28.1 with New York law and align with 28.2; 28.3 escalation is acceptable.

24.1–24.4 already permit Customer assignment to Affiliates/successors, restrict Vendor assignment and bar Vendor repricing or termination on our change of control; confirm 13.3 licence transfer tracks Section 24 and that 24.3 does not undercut 24.1.

14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of Deliverables with only a revocable, term-limited licence to us — reverse to Customer ownership of paid-for Deliverables (or at minimum the perpetual paid-up licence in 13.2). 14.1/15.1 correctly keep Customer Data ownership; check Deliverable/Vendor Technology definitions in 1.4 and 1.8 for scope creep.

13.1–13.3 extend rights to Affiliates and contractors and limit revocation/suspension — acceptable. The problem is the revocable, non-transferable Deliverable licence in 14.2, which conflicts with the perpetual paid-up grant in 13.2; resolve in our favour.

22.1–22.3 already limit audits to once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, off-site where practicable, Vendor-borne cost absent >5% underpayment, with no direct system access; confirm nothing in Section 23 (records/assurance) creates a broader audit of Customer.

No liquidated damages or penalty payable by Customer is apparent; 7.3 bars interest on amounts not due and 27.3/19.4 give us credits/refunds. Closest exposure is the take-or-pay shortfall in 2.1, which functions as a penalty — address there. No SLA credit exhibit is in the outline; confirm service credits exist.

19.1–19.3 give professional-services, conformity, malicious-code and compliance warranties with a 90-day Deliverable period and term-long hosted conformity; 19.4 provides re-perform/refund plus termination and is non-exclusive for IP, security and indemnified claims. Confirm 90 days is adequate and that 19.5's disclaimer does not erode express warranties.

18.1 carries CGL, workers' comp, employer's liability, E&O and USD 5M cyber cover for the term plus one year, and 18.2 confirms certificates and that insurance does not limit liability; check cyber limits against our PHI/data exposure under Sections 15 and 17.

2.1 imposes a USD 2,000,000 per year three-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination rights — our top-priority fix: delete or add exit/reduction rights and credit for terminated Services. Note conflict with 12.3's no-minimum-volume acknowledgement and with the termination rights in Section 9.

Section 10 addresses access cut-off, Deliverable delivery and refunds but the outline shows no data-return/export obligation or transition-assistance commitment (no 10.3+ and no 11 present, though 16.5 cross-references Sections 11 and 15). Add extraction of Customer Data in a usable format plus priced transition services at sec-10.
